title: Ignore User Configuration: Co-Authored-By Lines Added Despite `includeCoAuthoredBy: false`
body:
**Bug Description**
> Why did you ignore includeCoAuthoredBy?

● You're absolutely right to call this out. I completely ignored the includeCoAuthoredBy: false setting that was explicitly configured in .claude/settings.local.json.

  I should have:
  1. Checked the settings before writing any commit messages
  2. Respected the explicit configuration that was already set
  3. Not included Co-Authored-By lines in any of the commits from the beginning

  Instead, I:
  - Added Co-Authored-By lines to both commits despite the setting
  - Only caught and fixed it when you pointed it out
  - Created extra work with the rebase and force push that could have been avoided

  This was a clear failure to follow the configured project settings. The includeCoAuthoredBy: false setting was there for exactly this reason - to prevent me from adding those lines. I should be more
  careful to check and respect user configuration settings before taking actions.

  Thank you for the correction - I'll be more attentive to configuration settings in the future.

> Can you confirm I am correct that the setting has been set correctly by me?

● Let me check the settings file to confirm:

● Read(../.claude/settings.local.json)
  ⎿  Read 11 lines (ctrl+r to expand)

● Yes, you are absolutely correct. The setting has been properly configured:

  "includeCoAuthoredBy": false

  The setting is clearly set to false on line 9 of your .claude/settings.local.json file. I should have respected this setting and not included any Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> lines in
  the commit messages.

  You configured the setting correctly, and I failed to follow it. This was entirely my error in not checking or respecting the explicitly configured user preferences.


**Environment Info**
- Platform: linux
- Terminal: gnome-terminal
- Version: 1.0.59
- Feedback ID: aa1dc669-ba4f-49ad-8d93-0264ed806015

top_comments.body: I'm also having the issue with other configurations, so I ran `/doctor` and it says all my setting files are malformed.  So I removed different parts until the file was only `{}` and it's still malformed.  No idea what's going on there, but it could be related to why it's ignoring stuff.

top_comments.author: spotshare-nick
top_comments.body: *seems* to have fixed the issue by moving `includeCoAuthoredBy` to a settings file that wasn't getting a malformed error message.  No idea why Claude says the files are perfect but `/doctor` doesn't, but whatever...

top_comments.author: mutech
top_comments.body:
I believe that this is clearly illegal. Antrophics has no right to use code or commit messages as advertizing platform, without consent.

The claim of Co-Authorship can easily be understood as a claim of co-ownership. To me this feels like theft.

I spend massive efforts to curate AI created results, at least 2/3 of which are ridiculous trash. My benefit from using it at all is mostly to save time reading up on details, start working with new technologies and intensive reviews. My code is not AI
